accounting.headline: Accounting & Financial Services · Spanish · Core
accounting.threshold: Use Spanish to complete the core accounting & financial services conversations and explain the next step.

lessons.title: Collect records for a new client
lessons.objective: Explain your role to a new client and request a scoped set of records in Spanish, using que with the subjunctive to make a request.
lessons.focus: Necesitamos que plus the subjunctive to request documents, and the scope words solo, todos and los de.

words.note: Any written or digital entry of a transaction or document.
The complete set of records for a task or a client.
The item that needs attention first.
The defined limits of the work to be done.
Account summary from the bank for a period.
A summary of sales for a period.
A business that sells goods or services to the client.
A written agreement between two parties.
The system and list of wages paid to employees. Planilla is used in some Latin American countries.
An independent review of records and statements.

words.es: Necesitamos que nos envíe los extractos bancarios.
words.en: We need you to send us the bank statements.

words.es: ¿Cuál es la prioridad para este mes?
words.en: What is the priority for this month?

words.es: Empecemos por los extractos de los últimos seis meses.
words.en: Let's start with the bank statements from the last six months.

words.es: Solo necesitamos los documentos del año fiscal.
words.en: We only need the documents for the tax year.

words.es: Confirmo el alcance del servicio por escrito.
words.en: I confirm the scope of the service in writing.

lessons.speaking: Explain to a new restaurant owner what you will handle, then ask for a defined set of records: the last six months of bank statements, sales reports and supplier invoices. Confirm which item is the client's priority and agree when the set will be delivered.
lessons.partnerRole: New restaurant owner who wants to start with the most urgent records and does not yet know what the accountant needs.
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Soy el dueño del restaurante. ¿Por dónde empezamos?

grammar.focus: After necesitar, pedir or recomendar, a request for someone else's action takes que plus the present subjunctive: Necesitamos que envíe los extractos. When the subject is the same person, use the infinitive: necesito enviar.

examples.es: Necesitamos que nos envíe los extractos de los últimos seis meses.
examples.en: We need you to send us the bank statements for the last six months.

examples.es: Necesito enviar la lista de proveedores hoy.
examples.en: I need to send the list of suppliers today.

lessons.title: Classify business transactions
lessons.objective: Classify a business purchase in Spanish by its category and purpose, using por and para correctly.
lessons.focus: Por for cause, route and exchange, and para for purpose, recipient and deadline, with a categorized purchase.

words.note: The category given to a transaction in the accounts.
A long-lasting item used in the business, such as an oven.
A cost to keep an existing asset working.
An item or service bought by the business.
The account in which an expense is recorded.
The gradual reduction in an asset's recorded value over time.
Work that restores an item to working condition.
A plan of expected revenue and costs. It also means a written quote from a supplier.
The reason a purchase is made.
A document that proves a transaction, such as a receipt or invoice.

words.es: El horno es para la cocina principal.
words.en: The oven is for the main kitchen.
We paid 4,500 euros for the oven.
words.note: Por expresses the exchange: money for an item.

words.es: ¿Es una reparación o una compra de activo fijo?
words.en: Is it a repair or a fixed asset purchase?

lessons.speaking: Discuss a kitchen oven purchase with the owner. Confirm its category, ask what it is for, and decide whether it is a repair or a new asset. Repeat the category and the purpose, then agree the next step.
lessons.partnerRole: Restaurant owner who bought a new oven and wants to know how it will appear in the accounts.
lessons.openingLine: Compré un horno nuevo para la cocina. ¿Cómo lo debo registrar?

grammar.focus: Por marks exchange or cause: pagué 4.500 euros por el horno (in exchange for the oven). Para marks purpose, recipient or deadline: el horno es para la cocina; lo necesito para el viernes.

examples.es: Pagamos 4.500 euros por el horno.
examples.en: We paid 4,500 euros for the oven.

examples.es: El horno es para la cocina principal.
examples.en: The oven is for the main kitchen.

lessons.title: Record a journal entry
lessons.objective: Explain in Spanish what a journal entry records, confirm its date, amount and evidence, and use the impersonal se in an accounting description.
lessons.focus: Impersonal and passive se with registrar, and the recorded amount agreed with the supporting document.

words.note: A record of debits and credits for one transaction.
One line of an entry or a document.
The left column of an entry.
The right column of an entry.
The date on which a transaction is recorded in the books.
A money figure on a document.
Evidence that supports a recorded transaction.
An account number or name in the accounts.
To record a transaction in the accounts.
A check of a record before it is posted or closed.

words.es: Se registra el pago en la cuenta del proveedor.
words.en: The payment is recorded in the supplier's account.
Does the amount match the supporting document?

words.es: Confirma la fecha contable antes de contabilizar.
words.en: Please confirm the accounting date before posting.
words.note: Tú command, usual between coworkers. With a client: confirme.

words.es: Se contabilizan los asientos al cierre del día.
words.en: The entries are posted at the end of the day.

lessons.speaking: Walk a coworker through a supplier payment entry. Name the date, the amount, the debit and credit accounts and the supporting document, then ask the coworker to confirm before posting.
lessons.partnerRole: Coworker who reviews entries before they are posted to the ledger.
lessons.openingLine: Tengo que registrar un asiento del pago al proveedor. ¿Me confirmas los datos?

grammar.focus: Se with a third-person verb describes what is done without naming the agent: se registra el asiento (the entry is recorded). Use se in impersonal or passive form when the actor is unknown or unimportant. Agreement follows the thing recorded: se registran los pagos.

examples.es: Se registra el pago en la cuenta del proveedor.
examples.en: The payment is recorded in the supplier's account.

examples.es: Se registran los asientos cada día.
examples.en: The entries are recorded every day.

lessons.title: Read a ledger with a coworker
lessons.objective: Read a ledger with a coworker in Spanish and explain how an entry changed an account, using the imperfect for a past state and the preterite for an event.
lessons.focus: Imperfect (era, estaba, tenía) for an ongoing or prior state and preterite (llegó, pagó) for a completed event.

words.note: The record of every account and its movements.
A recorded line in a ledger.
The balance at the start of a period.
The balance at the end of a period.
A change posted to an account.
Money owed to the business by its clients.
Money received against an amount owed.
Money paid out or applied to a bill.
To match one record against another.
A change to correct or update a balance.

words.es: ¿Cuál era el saldo antes del asiento?
words.en: What was the balance before the entry?

lessons.speaking: Read one ledger line with a coworker. Explain what the balance was before the entry, what the entry changed, and what the balance is now. Confirm the figures back to the coworker, then agree the review.
lessons.partnerRole: Coworker reviewing a ledger line after an entry was posted.
lessons.openingLine: Hay una entrada en el libro mayor que no entiendo. ¿Podemos verla juntos?

grammar.focus: The imperfect describes a state that continued in the past: el saldo era 5.000 euros (the balance was). The preterite marks a completed event that changed it: el pago llegó ayer (the payment arrived yesterday). Use both in one story: el saldo era alto cuando llegó el pago.

examples.es: El saldo era de 5.000 euros cuando llegó el pago.
examples.en: The balance was 5,000 euros when the payment arrived.

examples.es: El pago llegó ayer y el saldo bajó a 3.800 euros.
examples.en: The payment arrived yesterday and the balance dropped to 3,800 euros.

lessons.title: Match an invoice to a payment
lessons.objective: Compare an invoice number, payment reference, date and amount in Spanish and explain any mismatch, using the present perfect for an action just completed.
lessons.focus: Present perfect (he comparado, ha llegado) for completed actions linked to now, and the mismatch vocabulary.

words.note: The identifier printed on the invoice.
The code or note that links a payment to an invoice.
A money figure on a document.
The date on which funds count for interest or availability.
A difference between two records that should match.
The act of matching records.
Money received against an invoice.
An invoice still unpaid or unmatched.
Evidence from the bank that a payment was sent or received.
A bank account for daily payments.

words.es: He comparado el número de factura con la referencia.
words.en: I have compared the invoice number with the reference.
Does the amount match the invoice?

words.es: El pago ya ha llegado con otra fecha.
words.en: The payment has already arrived with a different date.

words.es: La referencia no coincide con la factura.
words.en: The reference does not match the invoice.

lessons.speaking: Match an invoice to a payment with a client. Compare the number, reference, date and amount aloud, report which fields match, and name the one that does not. Agree on the next check.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who thinks an invoice was paid but the bank shows a different reference.
lessons.openingLine: Pagamos la factura del mes pasado, pero ustedes la tienen como pendiente. ¿Puede verificarlo?

grammar.focus: The present perfect uses haber (he, has, ha) plus the past participle: he comparado (I have compared), ha llegado (it has arrived). It describes an action completed that is relevant now. The participle of -ar verbs ends in -ado and of -er and -ir verbs in -ido.

examples.es: He comparado el número de factura con la referencia del banco.
examples.en: I have compared the invoice number with the bank reference.

examples.es: El pago ya ha llegado, pero con otra fecha.
examples.en: The payment has already arrived, but with a different date.

lessons.title: Follow up on an unpaid invoice
lessons.objective: Ask a client in Spanish when an unpaid invoice will be paid and agree how to resolve a disputed item, using espero que with the subjunctive.
lessons.focus: Espero que plus the subjunctive for a hoped-for payment, and the future for a firm commitment.

words.note: An invoice past its due date.
A line item the client disagrees with.
The part of the amount the client accepts.
The date the payment is expected.
A message asking for payment.
The time allowed to pay an invoice.
Interest charged on an overdue invoice where the law or contract allows.
A plan with agreed dates for paying an amount.
A service that was billed but not provided.
The person or business that owes the payment.

words.en: When do you expect to pay the invoice?

words.es: Espero que el pago llegue antes del viernes.
words.en: I hope the payment arrives before Friday.

words.es: Pagaremos la parte no disputada el lunes.
words.en: We will pay the undisputed part on Monday.
We will review that line separately.

lessons.speaking: Follow up on an invoice more than thirty days old. Ask for the expected payment date, name the disputed line, and agree whether the client will pay the undisputed part now and review the dispute separately. Close with the agreed date.
lessons.partnerRole: Client with a late invoice who disputes one line for a service that was not delivered.
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días, llamo por la factura de hace un mes. ¿Cuándo espera pagarla?

grammar.focus: Espero que (I hope that) takes the subjunctive when the outcome depends on someone else: espero que pague pronto. The future tense expresses a firm promise: pagaré el viernes. Use the subjunctive after es importante que as well: es importante que revise la línea.

examples.es: Espero que el cliente pague antes del viernes.
examples.en: I hope the client pays before Friday.

examples.es: Pagaré la parte no disputada el lunes.
examples.en: I will pay the undisputed part on Monday.

lessons.title: Review bills before paying
lessons.objective: Confirm the payee, due date, approval and amount of a bill in Spanish before payment is authorized, using cuando with the subjunctive for a future trigger.
lessons.focus: Cuando plus the subjunctive for a future event (cuando apruebe, cuando llegue), and se with a passive for an approval rule.

words.note: The person or business that receives the payment.
The day a payment must be made.
The authorization that allows a payment to proceed.
The money figure on the bill.
A document requesting payment for goods or services.
A group of payments released together.
The instruction that authorizes a payment.
An amount held back from a payment for tax or other reasons, where applicable.
A formal permission to pay or spend.
A business that provides goods or services.

words.es: Pagaremos cuando usted apruebe la factura.
words.en: We will pay when you approve the invoice.

words.es: ¿Quién es el beneficiario de este pago?
words.en: Who is the payee of this payment?

words.es: No se paga ninguna factura sin aprobación.
words.en: No invoice is paid without approval.

words.es: Confirme el importe y la fecha de vencimiento.
words.en: Please confirm the amount and the due date.

lessons.speaking: Review three supplier bills with the owner before any are paid. For each bill, confirm the payee, due date, approval and amount, then say which bill will be paid first and under what condition. Close by stating when the payment run will be authorized.
lessons.partnerRole: Restaurant owner who must approve each supplier bill before the payment run.
lessons.openingLine: Tengo tres facturas de proveedores. ¿Cuál debemos pagar primero?

grammar.focus: Cuando (when) takes the subjunctive when the event is in the future and not yet confirmed: pagaremos cuando usted apruebe la factura. Use the indicative for a habit or past fact: pagamos cuando llega la factura. Se with a passive verb states a general approval rule: no se paga ninguna factura sin aprobación.

examples.es: Pagaremos la factura cuando usted la apruebe.
examples.en: We will pay the invoice when you approve it.

examples.es: Pagamos cada factura cuando llega al despacho.
examples.en: We pay each invoice when it arrives at the office.

lessons.title: Reconcile a bank statement
lessons.objective: Explain in Spanish why a bank statement and a ledger differ, and name the outstanding items, using se debe a for cause and de with the verbs of the bank.
lessons.focus: Se debe a for the cause of a difference, and expressions with cheques pendientes, cargos and abonos not yet posted.

words.note: The process of matching a bank statement to the ledger.
A check written but not yet cleared by the bank.
A transaction in the ledger or statement that has not yet appeared on the other side.
A sum added to an account.
A sum taken from an account.
The gap between two figures.
The balance shown by the bank.
The balance shown in the ledger.
A correction made in the ledger.
The summary of the bank account for a period.

words.es: La diferencia se debe a dos cheques pendientes.
words.en: The difference is due to two outstanding checks.

words.es: El saldo bancario no coincide con el contable.
words.en: The bank balance does not match the book balance.

words.es: ¿Cuáles son las partidas pendientes de este mes?
words.en: What are the outstanding items for this month?

words.es: Registramos el ajuste después de revisar el extracto.
words.en: We record the adjustment after reviewing the statement.

lessons.speaking: Explain to a coworker why the bank balance and the ledger balance differ. Name two outstanding items, say what each one is, and state the cause of the total difference. Ask the coworker to confirm the adjusted figure.
lessons.partnerRole: Coworker who has to explain the difference to the owner before lunch.
lessons.openingLine: El extracto dice una cifra y el libro mayor otra. ¿Por qué no coinciden?

grammar.focus: Deberse a means to be due to. The verb agrees with the thing being explained: la diferencia se debe a dos cheques; las diferencias se deben a dos cheques. On a statement, cargos take money out and abonos put money in.

examples.es: La diferencia se debe a dos cheques pendientes de cobro.
examples.en: The difference is due to two uncleared checks.

examples.es: El banco aún no registró el abono de la transferencia.
examples.en: The bank has not yet recorded the transfer credit.

lessons.title: Discuss a bookkeeping correction
lessons.objective: Describe a bookkeeping correction in Spanish with the original entry, the error and the fix, without blaming a colleague, using the pluperfect for a prior action.
lessons.focus: Pluperfect (había registrado) for an earlier action before another past event, and impersonal se for a neutral description of the error.

words.note: The first entry before a correction.
A change that fixes an error in the records.
A mistake in entering a transaction.
An entry that cancels an earlier entry. Spain often says contraasiento or asiento de anulación.
An item recorded more than once.
The right figure after review.
A written explanation of the change.
A check of an entry or record.
A balance after the correction.
The end of an accounting period.

words.es: El asiento original registró el importe dos veces.
words.en: The original entry recorded the amount twice.

words.es: Hacemos un asiento de reversión por el importe duplicado.
words.en: We make a reversing entry for the duplicated amount.

words.es: La nota de corrección explica el cambio.
words.en: The correction note explains the change.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el saldo revisado después del ajuste?
words.en: What is the revised balance after the adjustment?

lessons.speaking: Explain a correction to a coworker. Say what the original entry recorded, what the error was, and what the correction changes. Keep the description about the entry, not the person, and close by agreeing the revised figure.
lessons.partnerRole: Coworker who entered the original payment and wants to know the fix.
lessons.openingLine: Vi una corrección en el asiento del martes. ¿Qué pasó con el pago?

grammar.focus: The pluperfect uses había plus the participle for an action completed before another past action: el pago ya se había registrado cuando lo revisamos. Describe the error neutrally with se: se registró dos veces el mismo pago. Avoid naming the person who entered it.

examples.es: El pago ya se había registrado cuando lo revisamos.
examples.en: The payment had already been recorded when we reviewed it.

examples.es: Se registró dos veces el mismo importe.
examples.en: The same amount was recorded twice.

lessons.title: Explain a payroll statement
lessons.objective: Explain gross pay, deductions and net pay on a fictional payroll statement in Spanish, with the reflexive and passive se to describe how deductions apply.
lessons.focus: Passive se with descontar (se descuenta, se descuentan) and comparisons with menor que and más que, using a payslip from Spain.

words.note: Pay before deductions.
Pay after deductions, the amount transferred.
An amount subtracted from gross pay.
In Spain, cotización a la Seguridad Social. Aporte is common in parts of Latin America.
An amount withheld from pay for tax. On a payslip in Spain it is the IRPF withholding.
Hours worked beyond the agreed schedule.
The statement showing pay and deductions for a period.
The time covered by one payment.
A person who works under an employment relationship.
The system and list of wages.

words.es: El sueldo neto es menor que el bruto.
words.en: The net pay is less than the gross pay.

words.es: Se descuenta la cotización a la Seguridad Social.
words.en: The Social Security contribution is deducted.

words.es: ¿Coinciden las horas con el recibo de nómina?
words.en: Do the hours match the payslip?

words.es: El importe neto llega a su cuenta.
words.en: The net amount reaches your account.

lessons.speaking: Walk an employee through a fictional payroll statement. State gross pay, name two deductions and say which one is a social contribution, then give the net pay. Confirm the net figure and ask the employee if the statement matches the hours worked.
lessons.partnerRole: Employee who is comparing gross and net pay for the first time.
lessons.openingLine: ¿Por qué mi sueldo neto es menor que el bruto? No entiendo los descuentos.

grammar.focus: Passive se with descontar: the verb agrees with what is deducted: se descuenta la cotización; se descuentan las cotizaciones. Compare with menor que or mayor que: el neto es menor que el bruto.

examples.es: Se descuentan las cotizaciones del salario bruto.
examples.en: The contributions are deducted from the gross salary.

examples.es: El sueldo neto es menor que el sueldo bruto.
examples.en: The net salary is less than the gross salary.

lessons.title: Distinguish contractor and employee records
lessons.objective: Ask in Spanish which documents describe a working arrangement, distinguishing a self-employed contractor from an employee, using ser and estar and the labeled jurisdiction.
lessons.focus: Ser for a classification (es autónoma, es empleada) and estar for a current status (está en nómina, el contrato está vigente), with an example from Spain.

words.note: A person or business that performs work under a service agreement.
A person working under an employment contract.
A person who works for their own account, the term used in Spain and some other countries.
An agreement for a defined service rather than employment.
An agreement that creates an employment relationship.
An invoice a contractor issues for work performed.
The list of employees paid through wages.
A contract or rule that currently applies.
The decision about whether a worker is an employee or a contractor.
The records that describe the arrangement.

words.es: ¿Es empleada o trabaja por cuenta propia?
words.en: Is she an employee or does she work for her own account?

words.es: Necesitamos el contrato y las facturas de servicios.
words.en: We need the contract and the services invoices.

words.es: El contrato está vigente desde enero.
words.en: The contract has been in force since January.

words.es: La clasificación depende de la jurisdicción.
words.en: The classification depends on the jurisdiction.

lessons.speaking: Ask a client whether a worker is self-employed or on payroll. Request the contract and the invoices for that worker, then identify the next review step for classification. Close by agreeing what the client will send.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who hires a freelance designer and is not sure whether the designer is a contractor or an employee.
lessons.openingLine: Contratamos a una diseñadora gráfica. ¿Es empleada o trabaja por cuenta propia?

grammar.focus: Ser classifies: es autónoma, es empleada. Estar gives a current status or result: está en nómina, está dada de alta, el contrato está vigente. In Spain, autónomo is the usual label for a self-employed worker.

examples.es: La diseñadora es autónoma y factura sus servicios.
examples.en: The designer is self-employed and invoices for her services.

examples.es: El contrato de la empleada está vigente desde enero.
examples.en: The employee's contract has been in force since January.

lessons.title: Read an income statement
lessons.objective: Explain revenue, expenses and profit as separate quantities for a reporting period in Spanish, using mayor que, menor que, tan ... como and tanto como.
lessons.focus: Comparatives mayor que and menor que with income statement quantities, tan ... como with adjectives and tanto como with verbs.

words.note: Money earned from sales or services in a period.
Costs incurred in a period.
What remains after expenses are subtracted from revenue. Common in Latin America; Spain usually says beneficio.
A report of revenue, expenses and profit for a period.
The time covered by the report.
The share of revenue that remains as profit.
The direct cost of the goods or services sold.
A cost of running the business that is not a direct cost of sales.
Sales after returns and discounts.
The outcome, such as a profit or loss.

words.es: Los ingresos son mayores que los gastos.

words.en: We did not earn as much as we expected.
words.note: Tanto como follows a verb. With an adjective use tan ... como.

words.en: What does the income statement include?

words.es: El margen es menor este trimestre.
words.en: The margin is lower this quarter.

lessons.speaking: Walk an owner through a simple income statement for a fictional bakery. Name revenue, expenses and profit for the quarter, compare two quantities with a comparative, then state what the profit does and does not show. Agree the next question.
lessons.partnerRole: Bakery owner who wants to know whether the business is profitable this quarter.
lessons.openingLine: ¿El trimestre salió bien? Quiero saber si ganamos más de lo que gastamos.

grammar.focus: With ser and quantities, use mayor que and menor que: los ingresos son mayores que los gastos. Tan plus an adjective plus como compares qualities: tan altas como. Tanto como follows a verb: no ganamos tanto como esperábamos.

examples.es: Los ingresos del trimestre son mayores que los gastos.
examples.en: Revenue for the quarter is greater than expenses.

examples.es: No ganamos tanto como esperábamos.
examples.en: We did not earn as much as we expected.

lessons.title: Read a balance sheet
lessons.objective: Explain assets, liabilities and equity on a fictional business balance sheet in Spanish, using es igual a and the verb tener to show what the business owns and owes.
lessons.focus: Balance equation expressed with es igual a and tener for ownership, with activo, pasivo and patrimonio.

words.note: Something the business owns or controls that has value.
An obligation the business owes to others.
The owners' share after liabilities are subtracted from assets. On a balance sheet in Spain it appears as patrimonio neto.
A snapshot of assets, liabilities and equity at a date. Estado de situación financiera is used in some countries.
An asset expected to be used or converted within a year.
A long-lived asset such as equipment or a building.
An obligation due within a year.
Money borrowed under agreed terms.
Money held in hand or in a bank account for immediate use.
Capital contributed by the owners of a company.

words.es: El activo total es igual al pasivo más el patrimonio.
words.en: Total assets equal liabilities plus equity.

words.es: El pasivo corriente vence este año.
words.en: The current liabilities fall due this year.

lessons.speaking: Teach a new owner what a fictional balance sheet shows. Name one asset, one liability and the equity figure, state the equation in Spanish, then ask the owner to repeat what the business owns and what it owes.
lessons.partnerRole: New owner of a small shop who wants to understand the balance sheet before the bank meeting.
lessons.openingLine: El balance tiene muchos números. ¿Qué significa cada columna para mí?

grammar.focus: Es igual a introduces the balance equation: activo es igual a pasivo más patrimonio. Tener (to have) states what the business holds, as in la empresa tiene un horno; deber or pasivo states what it owes. Use the plural when more than one item appears: los activos son mayores.

examples.es: El activo total es igual al pasivo más el patrimonio.
examples.en: Total assets equal liabilities plus equity.

examples.es: La empresa tiene un horno nuevo y debe 12.000 euros al banco.
examples.en: The company has a new oven and owes the bank 12,000 euros.

lessons.title: Discuss cash flow
lessons.objective: Explain in Spanish why recorded profit and cash available can differ, using aunque with the indicative and no es lo mismo que.
lessons.focus: Aunque with the indicative for a concession, no es lo mismo que for a contrast, and the cash-flow nouns.

words.note: The movement of cash into and out of the business over a period.
The recorded result after expenses.
Money that can be used now.
An amount a client owes to the business.
An amount the business owes a supplier.
A sale recorded but not yet paid.
A payment set for a date.
The money needed to cover daily operations.
The ability to pay obligations as they come due.
Money set aside for a future need.

words.es: Aunque ganamos dinero, no tenemos efectivo suficiente.
words.en: Although we made money, we do not have enough cash.

words.es: La utilidad no es lo mismo que el efectivo disponible.
words.en: Profit is not the same as the cash available.

words.es: Hay un cobro pendiente de la semana pasada.
words.en: There is a collection outstanding from last week.

words.es: ¿Qué pagos están programados para este mes?
words.en: Which payments are scheduled for this month?

lessons.speaking: Explain to an owner why a profitable month can leave no cash for a payment. Name one sale that was not yet collected and one payment that is due, then say what the owner should watch next. Ask the owner to repeat the difference between profit and cash.
lessons.partnerRole: Owner who sees profit on the report and cannot understand why the bank balance is low.
lessons.openingLine: El mes salió con utilidad, pero no tengo dinero para pagar al proveedor. ¿Cómo puede ser?

grammar.focus: Aunque (although) with the indicative states a fact that is true despite the other fact: aunque ganamos, no tenemos efectivo. No es lo mismo que contrasts two things that look alike: la utilidad no es lo mismo que el efectivo disponible.

examples.es: Aunque la empresa ganó dinero, no tiene efectivo para pagar.
examples.en: Although the company made money, it has no cash to pay.

examples.es: La utilidad no es lo mismo que el efectivo disponible.
examples.en: Profit is not the same as the cash available.

lessons.title: Plan a business budget
lessons.objective: Ask in Spanish about expected revenue, recurring costs and a planned purchase for a business budget, using the future and the first conditional.
lessons.focus: Future tense (venderemos, gastaremos) and si plus present for a plan that depends on a condition (si vendemos, podremos).

words.note: A plan of expected revenue and costs for a period.
Revenue the plan expects to earn.
Costs that do not change with sales volume, such as rent. Spain also says costes fijos.
Costs that change with sales volume, such as fuel for deliveries.
A purchase included in the budget before it is made.
An expectation the plan depends on.
One possible case the plan is tested against.
Cash coming in and going out over a period.
A light commercial van, the usual word in Spain. Much of Latin America says camioneta.
A transfer of goods to a customer.

words.en: How much do we expect to sell next quarter?

words.es: Si vendemos más, podremos comprar la furgoneta.
words.en: If we sell more, we will be able to buy the van.

words.es: Vamos a revisar el presupuesto a fin de mes.
words.en: We are going to review the budget at month end.

words.es: El supuesto principal es el volumen de entregas.
words.en: The main assumption is the volume of deliveries.

lessons.speaking: Plan next quarter's budget with a client who wants to buy a new delivery van. Ask about expected revenue and recurring costs, state two assumptions, and say what the business can afford if sales rise. Close by agreeing to review the plan at the end of the month.
lessons.partnerRole: Owner of a delivery business in Spain who wants to know whether the budget can support a van purchase.
lessons.openingLine: Quiero comprar una furgoneta para las entregas. ¿Cómo lo planeamos?

grammar.focus: The future adds endings to the infinitive: venderemos, gastaremos. A real condition uses si plus the present, then the future: si vendemos más, podremos comprar la furgoneta. Ir a plus an infinitive states a plan: vamos a revisar.

examples.es: Venderemos más si abrimos el servicio de entregas.
examples.en: We will sell more if we open the delivery service.

examples.es: Vamos a comprar una furgoneta cuando el presupuesto lo permita.
examples.en: We are going to buy a van when the budget allows it.

lessons.title: Explain a budget variance
lessons.objective: Compare a planned amount with an actual amount in Spanish and ask why the difference occurred, using porque and debido a, and the phrase superior a.
lessons.focus: Porque with indicative for cause, debido a for a noun cause, and comparative superior a or inferior a for variance.

words.note: The difference between planned and actual amounts.
The amount actually spent.
The amount planned in the budget.
Gasoline or diesel used by vehicles.
A departure from the plan.
The reason for a difference.
A change made to correct the plan or the record.
An amount above the budget. Spain also says sobrecoste.
One item in a budget or report.
An updated estimate of the future.

words.es: El gasto real es superior al presupuestado.
words.en: The actual expense is higher than budgeted.

words.es: ¿Cuál es la causa de la variación?
words.en: What is the cause of the variance?

words.es: El gasto subió porque el combustible costó más.
words.en: The expense rose because fuel cost more.

words.es: Revisaremos el pronóstico la próxima semana.
words.en: We will review the forecast next week.

lessons.speaking: Walk a manager through a monthly budget variance for delivery costs. Compare the planned and actual amounts, state the cause of the difference, and ask whether the variance will continue next month. Close by agreeing the corrective step.
lessons.partnerRole: Manager who expected lower delivery costs and sees an overrun.
lessons.openingLine: Los gastos de entregas están por encima del presupuesto. ¿Qué pasó este mes?

grammar.focus: Porque with the indicative gives a cause: el gasto subió porque el combustible costó más. Debido a plus a noun gives a formal cause: debido al precio del combustible. Superior a and inferior a compare a figure to a benchmark: el gasto real es superior al presupuesto.

examples.es: El gasto subió porque el combustible costó más de lo previsto.
examples.en: The expense rose because fuel cost more than expected.

examples.es: El gasto real es superior al presupuestado debido al precio del combustible.
examples.en: The actual expense is higher than budgeted due to the price of fuel.

lessons.title: Prepare a monthly client update
lessons.objective: Summarize results, unresolved questions and the next action for a client in a short monthly update written in Spanish, using the present perfect for work completed to date.
lessons.focus: Present perfect (hemos recibido, hemos revisado) for completed work and a future next-action statement with vamos a.

words.note: A short client update on results and open items. Resumen mensual is also used.
An outcome for the period.
An unresolved issue that needs a client answer.
The next step with a responsible person and a date.
A written account of results.
The person receiving the update.
A bill for services or goods.
Account summary for a period.
Matching of two records.
The last date for an action.

words.es: Hemos recibido todos los extractos del mes.
words.en: We have received all the statements for the month.

words.es: Queda una pregunta pendiente sobre una factura.
words.en: One question remains open about an invoice.

words.es: Vamos a enviar el informe final el jueves.
words.en: We are going to send the final report on Thursday.

words.es: ¿Podría confirmarnos esta información antes de la fecha límite?
words.en: Could you confirm this information before the deadline?

lessons.speaking: Read a short monthly update to a client. Summarize two results, name one unresolved question and state the next action with a date. Ask the client to confirm the update and any correction before sending.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who will receive the monthly update and wants a clear summary before the next call.
lessons.openingLine: ¿Me puede enviar un resumen del mes con lo que queda pendiente?

grammar.focus: The present perfect with haber and the participle shows work completed by now: hemos recibido todos los extractos. Use it for the month to date. Vamos a plus infinitive states the next action in a plain summary: vamos a enviar el informe el jueves.

examples.es: Hemos recibido todos los extractos del mes y hemos revisado las facturas.
examples.en: We have received all the statements for the month and reviewed the invoices.

examples.es: Vamos a enviar el informe final el jueves.
examples.en: We are going to send the final report on Thursday.

lessons.title: Discuss a loan application
lessons.objective: Ask a lender in Spanish about the purpose and requested amount of a loan and the documents the lender has requested, using quisiera and the conditional for a polite request.
lessons.focus: Quisiera (I would like) for a polite request, the conditional for a requested action, and para plus infinitive for purpose.

words.note: A formal request to borrow money.
The amount asked for in the loan application.
The time for repayment.
The reason the money is borrowed.
A financial institution that lends money.
The documents the lender asks for.
The statements that report the business position.
Something pledged to secure the loan.
The percentage charged on the loan.
The lender's decision to grant the loan.

words.es: Quisiera solicitar un préstamo para ampliar la panadería.
words.en: I would like to request a loan to expand the bakery.

words.es: ¿Qué documentos necesita el banco para revisar la solicitud?
words.en: What documents does the bank need to review the application?

words.es: El monto solicitado es de 25.000 euros.

words.en: Could you tell me the term you propose?

lessons.speaking: Open a loan conversation with a bank officer for a fictional bakery expansion. State the purpose of the loan, the requested amount and the term, then ask which documents the bank needs. Close by confirming the next meeting.
lessons.partnerRole: Bank officer who reviews loan requests for small businesses and asks for documents.
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar con su solicitud de préstamo?

grammar.focus: Quisiera is a polite form of querer and frames the request: quisiera solicitar un préstamo (I would like to request a loan). The conditional (podría, necesitaría) softens a request further. Para plus infinitive gives purpose: un préstamo para comprar equipo.

examples.es: Quisiera solicitar un préstamo para ampliar la panadería.
examples.en: I would like to request a loan to expand the bakery.

examples.es: ¿Podría indicarme qué documentos necesita el banco?
examples.en: Could you tell me which documents the bank needs?

lessons.title: Explain a loan quote
lessons.objective: Compare principal, interest, term, fees and the payment schedule in a Spanish loan quote without confusing them, using tanto ... como and the verb pagar with a time phrase.
lessons.focus: Tanto ... como for two parts of a cost, anual and al año for a rate period, and cuota as the regular payment.

words.note: The amount borrowed, before interest is added.
The cost of borrowing money, usually shown as a rate.
The period over which the loan is repaid.
A one-time fee for setting up the loan.
The regular amount paid each month.
The table of payments and their split between capital and interest.
The yearly interest rate. Spain distinguishes TIN, the nominal rate, from TAE, the annual equivalent rate that includes some costs.
All payments added together, including fees and interest.
The part of each payment that reduces the capital owed.
A written offer with the terms of a loan.

words.es: ¿Cuánto es el costo total del préstamo?
words.en: What is the total cost of the loan?

words.es: La cuota mensual incluye capital e intereses.
words.en: The monthly payment includes capital and interest.

words.es: La comisión de apertura se paga una vez.
words.en: The arrangement fee is paid once.

words.es: ¿Cómo se reparte la cuota en el cronograma?
words.en: How is the payment split in the schedule?

lessons.speaking: Read a fictional loan quote with a client. Name the principal, the interest rate, the term and the fees, then say what the monthly payment covers. Ask the client to repeat the total cost of the loan, and agree the next question.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who receives a loan quote and sees a monthly payment that is higher than expected.
lessons.openingLine: Me dieron una cotización de préstamo, pero no entiendo cuánto voy a pagar al final.

grammar.focus: Tanto ... como joins two parts of a cost: tanto el capital como los intereses forman la cuota. A rate takes anual or al año: un interés del 6 % anual. Cuota is the regular payment; capital is the principal repaid, not interest.

examples.es: Tanto el capital como los intereses forman la cuota mensual.
examples.en: Both the principal and the interest make up the monthly payment.

examples.es: En esta cotización, el interés es del 6 % anual durante cinco años.
examples.en: In this quote, the interest is 6% a year for five years.

lessons.title: Clarify collateral and guarantees
lessons.objective: Ask in Spanish what a proposed collateral or guarantee covers and request its written terms, using the relative clause with lo que and que with the subjunctive.
lessons.focus: Lo que for a thing or amount described (lo que cubre la garantía) and que with the subjunctive when the referent is unknown or not yet identified.

words.note: A pledge of an asset or a third party to secure a loan.
A guarantee tied to a specific asset, such as equipment or property.
A promise by a third person to pay if the borrower cannot.
Machines or tools the business uses.
The date a guarantee or loan ends.
The conditions in a written document.
An estimate of the value of an asset.
The extent of protection the guarantee provides.
The person or business that receives the loan.
The person or institution that lends the money.

words.en: What exactly does the guarantee cover?

words.es: Necesitamos una garantía que cubra todo el préstamo.
words.en: We need a guarantee that covers the whole loan.
When does the equipment guarantee expire?

lessons.speaking: Discuss a guarantee with a lender who offers to accept equipment. Ask what the guarantee covers, what the lender needs in writing, and whether the guarantee expires. Close by agreeing the document you will receive and the date.
lessons.partnerRole: Lender who proposes equipment as a guarantee and explains the written terms.
lessons.openingLine: Podemos aceptar la garantía del equipo. ¿Qué quiere saber sobre ella?

grammar.focus: Lo que introduces a clause about a thing or amount: lo que cubre la garantía es el equipo. Que with the subjunctive describes an unknown item: busco una garantía que cubra el préstamo completo. Use the subjunctive after an indefinite antecedent such as una garantía que cubra.

examples.es: Quiero saber lo que cubre la garantía del equipo.
examples.en: I want to know what the equipment guarantee covers.

examples.es: Necesitamos una garantía que cubra todo el préstamo.
examples.en: We need a guarantee that covers the whole loan.

lessons.title: Discuss a business banking fee
lessons.objective: Locate a business bank fee in Spanish, ask what triggered it and explain the bank's stated next step, using the passive se and the verb cobrar with a cause.
lessons.focus: Passive se for bank practice (se cobra una comisión, se aplicó), porque and por for the cause, and the future for the bank's stated next step.

words.note: A charge by the bank for a service or condition.
A bank account for business transactions.
The lowest balance required to avoid a fee.
An amount taken from the account.
A payment sent across borders.
A return of money paid.
A check of whether a fee applies correctly.
The bank contact for a business account.
The terms that govern the account.
The published price of a banking service.

words.es: ¿Qué motivó el cargo de la comisión?
La comisión se aplicó por saldo inferior al mínimo.
words.en: The fee was applied because the balance was below the minimum.

words.es: El banco responderá en tres días hábiles.
words.en: The bank will respond in three business days.

lessons.speaking: Call a bank officer about an unexpected fee on a business account. Ask what triggered the charge, what the bank's stated next step is, and whether the fee can be reversed. Close by confirming the date the bank will respond.
lessons.partnerRole: Bank officer who explains the fee and the policy for reversing it.
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes, banca de empresas, le atiende Jorge. ¿En qué puedo ayudarle?

grammar.focus: Se cobra describes the bank's practice without naming the agent: se cobra una comisión por transferencia. Por plus noun gives the cause: la comisión se aplica por la transferencia internacional. For a question about cause, use ¿por qué? or ¿qué causó?

examples.es: Se cobra una comisión cuando el saldo baja del mínimo.
examples.en: A fee is charged when the balance falls below the minimum.

examples.es: ¿Por qué se aplicó la comisión a nuestra cuenta de negocios?
examples.en: Why was the fee applied to our business account?

lessons.title: Prepare for a tax-document meeting
lessons.objective: Confirm the jurisdiction, reporting period and available documents before a tax-document meeting in Spanish, using the formal request forms of the verbs confirmar and preparar.
lessons.focus: Formal requests with usted (confirme, traiga, prepare) and the expression no olvide que to remind a client.

words.note: The authority whose tax rules apply.
The time covered by a tax report.
A formal filing to a tax authority. In Spain the personal income tax return is the declaración de la renta.
The annual period used for tax purposes.
Proof of payment for deductible or reportable items.
Records used for a tax filing.
The government body that collects tax. In Spain it is the Agencia Tributaria.
A professional who prepares or reviews tax filings.
The date by which a return must be submitted.
A duplicate of a document kept for the file.

words.es: Confirme la jurisdicción antes de la reunión.
words.en: Please confirm the jurisdiction before the meeting.

words.es: No olvide que necesitamos los recibos del año fiscal.
words.en: Do not forget that we need the receipts for the tax year.

words.es: ¿Qué documentos tiene disponibles para el periodo?
words.en: Which documents do you have available for the period?

words.es: Traiga la copia de la última declaración.
words.en: Bring a copy of the last return.

lessons.speaking: Confirm the details before a tax meeting with a client in Spain. Name the jurisdiction and tax year, the documents the client has ready and the one still missing. Close by asking the client to bring the missing items.
lessons.partnerRole: Client in Spain preparing for a meeting about her income tax return who is not sure which documents to bring.
lessons.openingLine: Mañana vemos mis documentos de impuestos. ¿Qué tengo que preparar?

grammar.focus: The usted command uses the present subjunctive form: confirme, traiga, prepare, revise. No olvide que plus a clause reminds a client of a requirement. Name the jurisdiction and year: en España, el año fiscal 2025.

examples.es: Confirme la jurisdicción y el periodo del informe antes de la reunión.
examples.en: Please confirm the jurisdiction and the reporting period before the meeting.

examples.es: No olvide que necesitamos los recibos del año fiscal.
examples.en: Do not forget that we need the receipts for the tax year.

lessons.title: Distinguish deductions and tax credits
lessons.objective: Distinguish a tax deduction from a tax credit in Spanish on a US federal return, with fictional round figures and the comparisons más que and menos que.
lessons.focus: Reduce la base versus reduce el impuesto, with vale más que and vale menos que for the difference in effect.

words.note: On a US return it lowers taxable income. In Spain's IRPF, deducción lowers the tax itself and reducción lowers the base.
An amount subtracted from the tax owed. IRS Spanish materials say crédito tributario; crédito fiscal is also common.
The amount on which tax is calculated.
The percentage applied to the taxable base.
The tax amount owed after credits.
A cost the tax rules allow to be deducted. Which costs qualify depends on the jurisdiction and the taxpayer.
The authority whose rules apply.
A teaching case that does not describe a real rule.
A decrease in an amount. In Spain's IRPF, reducciones lower the taxable base, while deducciones lower the tax itself.
The final calculation of tax owed.

words.es: Una deducción reduce la base imponible.
words.en: A deduction reduces the taxable base.

words.es: Un crédito reduce el impuesto directamente.
words.en: A credit reduces the tax directly.

words.es: Con la misma cifra, la deducción vale menos que el crédito.
words.en: For the same figure, the deduction is worth less than the credit.

words.es: Este es un ejemplo ficticio, no una regla real.
words.en: This is a fictional example, not a real rule.

lessons.speaking: Explain to a client in the United States, with fictional round figures, how a deduction and a credit reduce federal income tax differently. Give one example of each, state which one reduces the base and which reduces the tax itself, then check the client understands.
lessons.partnerRole: Client in Texas who thinks a deduction and a tax credit are the same thing.
lessons.openingLine: ¿La deducción y el crédito son lo mismo? Me confundo porque los dos bajan el impuesto.

grammar.focus: Una deducción reduce la base imponible, the amount tax is calculated on. Un crédito reduce el impuesto directamente. Compare effects with más que and menos que: vale menos que. Before a number use más de: más de 200 dólares.

examples.es: Una deducción reduce la base imponible; un crédito reduce el impuesto.
examples.en: A deduction reduces the taxable base; a credit reduces the tax itself.

examples.es: En este ejemplo, la deducción vale menos que un crédito del mismo importe.
examples.en: In this example, the deduction is worth less than a credit of the same amount.

lessons.title: Discuss estimated tax payments
lessons.objective: Explain in Spanish what period a quarterly advance tax payment in Spain covers and distinguish that estimate from the final IRPF liability, using the future and the present perfect.
lessons.focus: Future for a planned payment (pagaremos), present perfect for a completed period (hemos pagado), and the contrast between estimate and final amount.

words.note: In Spain, a quarterly IRPF advance many self-employed workers make. US Spanish says pago de impuesto estimado.
The tax owed once the year is settled.
The time the payment relates to.
The settled amount at the end of the period.
The yearly return that settles the final tax. In Spain, the declaración de la renta.
A correction after the final calculation.
A payment credited against the final tax for the year.
An amount the tax authority owes the taxpayer, where it applies.
An amount still owed after the estimates.
The date by which a payment must be made.

words.es: Esta cuota es una estimación, no el impuesto final.
words.en: This payment is an estimate, not the final tax.

words.es: Hemos pagado dos cuotas este año.
words.en: We have paid two installments this year.

words.es: Si hay saldo a pagar, lo pagaremos con la declaración anual.
words.en: If there is a balance due, we will pay it with the annual return.
Which period does this advance payment cover?

lessons.speaking: Explain to a self-employed client in Spain what the quarterly advance payment covers, whether it is final, and when the year is settled. Name the period covered and agree when you will prepare the annual return.
lessons.partnerRole: Self-employed client in Spain who has made a quarterly advance payment and wants to know whether it is the final tax.
lessons.openingLine: Hice el pago fraccionado del trimestre. ¿Ya terminé de pagar lo que debo?

grammar.focus: Use the future for a planned payment: pagaremos el saldo. Use the present perfect for a period that is still open: hemos pagado dos cuotas este año. In Spain a pago fraccionado is an advance on account; the final IRPF is settled in the annual return.

examples.es: Hemos pagado dos cuotas este año.
examples.en: We have paid two installments this year.

examples.es: Esta cuota es una estimación, no el impuesto final.
examples.en: This payment is an estimate, not the final tax.

lessons.title: Ask about investment income records
lessons.objective: Request statements in Spanish that show interest, distributions or realized sales from an investment account, using the subjunctive in a relative clause for an unknown document.
lessons.focus: Subjunctive in a relative clause with an indefinite antecedent (busco un extracto que muestre), and the vocabulary of investment income.

words.note: The periodic summary of holdings and transactions.
Income earned from deposits or debt securities.
Payments made to shareholders from a company's profits.
A sale that has closed and produced a gain or loss.
The profit from selling an asset for more than its cost.
The loss from selling an asset for less than its cost.
An account that holds securities or funds for investment.
The period for which income must be reported.
The original cost used to calculate a gain or loss, often including purchase fees.
A payment from a fund or partnership to its owners.

words.es: Necesito un extracto que muestre los intereses.
words.en: I need a statement that shows the interest.

words.es: ¿Qué ventas realizadas hubo en el periodo?
words.en: Which realized sales were there in the period?

words.es: El valor de adquisición aparece en el informe fiscal.
words.en: The cost basis appears on the tax report.

words.es: Solicito el extracto con los dividendos del año.
words.en: I request the statement with the dividends for the year.

lessons.speaking: Call a client's investment provider, or the client, and request a statement that shows interest, distributions and realized sales for the tax period. Confirm the period and the format, then agree when the document will arrive.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who holds an investment account and has not yet sent the annual income statement.
lessons.openingLine: Tengo una cuenta de inversión. ¿Qué papel necesita usted del año pasado?

grammar.focus: When a relative clause describes a document you have not yet located, use the subjunctive: busco un extracto que muestre los intereses (I am looking for a statement that shows the interest). With a known document, use the indicative: el extracto que recibí muestra los intereses.

examples.es: Necesito un extracto que muestre los intereses y los dividendos del año.
examples.en: I need a statement that shows the interest and dividends for the year.

examples.es: El extracto que recibí muestra los intereses del trimestre.
examples.en: The statement I received shows the quarter's interest.

lessons.title: Discuss cross-border records
lessons.objective: Confirm currencies, dates and source records for a cross-border transaction in Spanish, using the preposition en and the conversion expression al tipo de cambio.
lessons.focus: The expression al tipo de cambio de la fecha for converting an amount, and en plus currency for the currency of a record.

words.note: Any currency other than the one used for the books.
The price of one currency in another.
The date whose rate applies to the conversion.
The record or publication that supplies a figure.
The amount after conversion to the book currency.
A fee charged for converting currency.
A payment sent across borders.
A supplier located in another country.
A professional with specific expertise in one area.
The gain or loss when the rate on the payment date differs from the rate on the invoice date.

words.es: Registramos el pago al tipo de cambio de la fecha de pago.
words.en: We record the payment at the exchange rate on the payment date.

words.es: ¿Cuál es la fuente del tipo de cambio?
words.en: What is the source of the exchange rate?

words.es: Esta pregunta debe revisarla un especialista en impuestos internacionales.
words.en: This question should be reviewed by a specialist in international tax.

lessons.speaking: Explain to a client how a foreign-currency invoice will be recorded. Confirm the currency, the exchange rate date and the source records, then identify one question for the specialist in international tax. Close by agreeing who sends the final figure.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who receives payments from a foreign supplier and wants to know how the amounts are recorded.
lessons.openingLine: Recibimos una factura en dólares de un proveedor extranjero. ¿Cómo la registramos?

grammar.focus: En plus a currency names the currency of a record: la factura está en dólares. Al tipo de cambio de plus a date states which rate applies: la factura, al tipo de la fecha de factura; el pago, al de la fecha de pago.

examples.es: La factura está en dólares y la registramos al tipo de cambio de la fecha de factura.
examples.en: The invoice is in dollars, and we record it at the exchange rate on the invoice date.

examples.es: Necesitamos la fuente del tipo de cambio que usó el banco.
examples.en: We need the source of the exchange rate the bank used.

lessons.title: Explain an information request
lessons.objective: Explain in Spanish what an auditor or reviewer requested and agree who will provide it, using reported speech with que and the preterite of pedir.
lessons.focus: Reported speech with dijo que and pidió que plus the subjunctive, and the assignment of responsibility with encargarse de.

words.note: An independent reviewer outside the firm.
A formal request for records or explanations.
The person who owns a task.
Expression for assigning ownership of a task.
The date by which a reply is due.
A written list of records requested.
A point the reviewer notes.
A review of records and statements.
A document showing how a figure was prepared.
The answer to a request.

words.es: El revisor pidió que enviáramos el registro de nómina.
words.en: The reviewer asked us to send the payroll record.

words.es: Confirmo la fecha de respuesta por escrito.
words.en: I will confirm the response date in writing.

words.es: Esta solicitud de información es parte de la auditoría.
words.en: This information request is part of the audit.

lessons.speaking: Report to a colleague what the external reviewer asked for, in your own words. Name the three items requested, agree who will provide each one, and set a date for the response. Confirm the list back to the colleague.
lessons.partnerRole: Colleague who needs to know exactly what the reviewer asked for and who is responsible for each item.
lessons.openingLine: Recibí un correo del revisor externo. ¿Qué pidió exactamente?

grammar.focus: Reported speech uses dijo que (said that) and the indicative for a fact, but for a request the subjunctive follows pidió que: pidió que enviáramos los extractos. Encargarse de means to take responsibility for: me encargo de los extractos.

examples.es: El revisor dijo que necesitaba los extractos de todo el año.
examples.en: The reviewer said that he needed the statements for the whole year.

examples.es: El revisor pidió que enviáramos el registro de nómina.
examples.en: The reviewer asked us to send the payroll record.

lessons.title: Handoff work to a colleague
lessons.objective: Summarize in Spanish the checks completed, the open questions and the client communication already sent when handing off work to a colleague, using the present perfect for work done.
lessons.focus: Present perfect for completed checks (he revisado, hemos enviado) and the present for open items (queda, falta).

words.note: The complete set of records for a client.
The formal transfer of a task to another person.
A review step that has been finished.
An unresolved issue on a file.
A written communication sent to the client.
A message sent to the client.
The action that comes next.
A written summary left for the colleague.
The person who now owns the file.
The last check before closing a file.

words.es: He revisado los extractos del trimestre.
words.en: I have reviewed the quarter's statements.

words.es: Hemos enviado la carta al cliente.
words.en: We have sent the letter to the client.

words.es: Queda una pregunta abierta sobre la factura.
words.en: One open question remains about the invoice.

words.es: Te dejo la nota de traspaso con el próximo paso.
words.en: I am leaving you the handoff note with the next step.
words.note: Te for a colleague you address as tú; le with usted.

lessons.speaking: Hand off a client file to a colleague who starts tomorrow. Summarize the checks you have completed, name the one open question, and state what the client has already been told. Close by asking the colleague to repeat the next step.
lessons.partnerRole: Colleague taking over the file who needs a clear, organized summary.
lessons.openingLine: Mañana me hago cargo del expediente. ¿Qué está hecho y qué falta?

grammar.focus: The present perfect uses haber plus the participle for work completed by now: he revisado los extractos, hemos enviado la carta. The present tense shows what still exists: queda una pregunta, falta el recibo. A handoff needs both.

examples.es: He revisado los extractos y hemos enviado la carta al cliente.
examples.en: I have reviewed the statements and we have sent the letter to the client.

examples.es: Queda una pregunta abierta sobre la factura de marzo.
examples.en: One open question remains about the March invoice.

lessons.title: Protect client information in conversation
lessons.objective: Protect client information in a Spanish conversation by confirming the approved channel and declining to share passwords or access codes, using the negatives no and ni.
lessons.focus: Negation with no and ni (no le puedo dar la contraseña, ni por teléfono), the approved channel with por, and the polite refusal form.

words.note: A secret word or phrase used to access an account.
A code used to sign in or confirm a transaction.
The secure method agreed for sharing information.
An encrypted online service for sending documents.
Information that identifies a person.
A check that confirms who a caller is.
Deception used to obtain money or information.
A call the recipient did not expect.
Information that must not be shared.
A step-by-step method for a task.

words.es: No le puedo dar la contraseña ni el código.
words.en: I cannot give you the password or the code.

words.es: Confirmamos el pago por el portal seguro.
words.en: We confirm the payment through the secure portal.

words.es: Lo siento, pero no comparto datos personales por teléfono.
words.en: I am sorry, but I do not share personal data by phone.

words.es: Puede verificar su identidad en la oficina.
words.en: You can verify your identity at the office.

lessons.speaking: Respond to a caller who asks for an online banking password and a client access code. Decline politely, confirm the approved channel, and explain what you can do instead. Close by agreeing the secure route for the documents.
lessons.partnerRole: Caller who sounds urgent and asks for a password and a code to speed up a payment.
lessons.openingLine: Llamo del banco. Necesito la contraseña y el código para liberar el pago ahora mismo.

grammar.focus: Negation in Spanish uses no before the verb and allows double negatives: no le doy la contraseña, ni por teléfono ni por correo. Ni plus a noun adds to a negative: ni la contraseña ni el código. Use por for the channel: por el portal seguro. Refuse politely with lo siento, pero.

examples.es: No le puedo dar la contraseña ni el código por teléfono.
examples.en: I cannot give you the password or the code by phone.

examples.es: Confirmamos el pago por el portal seguro del banco.
examples.en: We confirm the payment through the bank's secure portal.

lessons.title: Complete a routine client case
lessons.objective: Take one routine client case from document intake to a written and spoken action summary in Spanish, combining receipt, check, question and next date.
lessons.focus: Integrated use of the preterite for completed actions, the present perfect for work done so far, the subjunctive for requests, and the future for the next step.

words.note: The complete set of records for a client.
The step where records are received and logged.
A review that confirms the work is complete and correct.
An item not yet resolved.
A list of what was done and what comes next.
The date by which an item is due.
The person who owns the next step.
Proof that a date or request was accepted.
The point at which the file is complete.
The action that comes next.

words.es: Hemos revisado casi todo el expediente.
words.en: We have reviewed almost all of the file.

words.es: Necesitamos que nos envíe el recibo pendiente.
words.en: We need you to send us the outstanding receipt.

words.es: Enviaremos el resumen de acciones el jueves.
words.en: We will send the action summary on Thursday.

lessons.speaking: Take a client file from intake to close. Say what was received, what was checked, one item still missing, and the next date. Ask the client to confirm the action summary, then send the agreed written summary.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who wants a short, complete action summary for a routine document review.
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Ya le envié los documentos del mes. ¿Qué pasa ahora?

grammar.focus: Combine the tenses already studied: the preterite recibí (received), the present perfect hemos revisado (we have reviewed), the subjunctive for a request necesitamos que envíe, and the future for the next step enviaremos el resumen. End with a date and a responsible person.

examples.es: Recibí los documentos de marzo, y hemos revisado casi todo.
examples.en: I received the March documents, and we have reviewed almost all of it.

examples.es: Necesitamos que nos envíe el recibo pendiente antes del jueves.
examples.en: We need you to send us the outstanding receipt before Thursday.

accounting-english.headline: Accounting & Financial Services · English · Core
accounting-english.threshold: Use English to complete the core accounting & financial services conversations and explain the next step.

lessons.title: Collect records for a new client
lessons.objective: Explicar tu función a un nuevo cliente y pedir un conjunto acotado de documentos en inglés, usando need + persona + to + verbo.
lessons.focus: Need someone to do, only y all the para acotar peticiones, y la diferencia entre need y needs en tercera persona.

words.note: Entrada escrita o digital de una operación o un documento.
Conjunto completo de registros para un trabajo o un cliente.
Lo que debe atenderse primero.
Límites definidos del trabajo que se va a hacer.
Resumen periódico de los movimientos de la cuenta.
Resumen de ventas en un periodo.
Empresa que vende bienes o servicios al cliente.
Acuerdo escrito entre dos partes.
Sistema y lista de salarios pagados a los empleados.
Revisión independiente de registros y estados financieros.

words.es: We need you to send the bank statements.
words.en: Necesitamos que nos envíe los extractos bancarios.

words.es: What is the priority this month?
words.en: ¿Cuál es la prioridad de este mes?

words.es: Let's start with the last six months of statements.
words.en: Empecemos por los extractos de los últimos seis meses.
words.note: Let's + forma base propone empezar juntos.

words.es: We only need the documents for the tax year.
words.en: Solo necesitamos los documentos del año fiscal.

words.es: I will confirm the scope in writing.
words.note: Will para una promesa de acción.

lessons.speaking: Explica a un dueño de restaurante qué vas a llevar y pide un conjunto de registros: extractos de los últimos seis meses, informes de ventas y facturas de proveedores. Confirma cuál es la prioridad y acuerda cuándo llegarán.
lessons.partnerRole: Dueño de restaurante nuevo que quiere empezar con lo más urgente y no sabe qué necesita el contador.
lessons.openingLine: Good afternoon. I own the restaurant. Where should we start?

grammar.focus: Need + persona + to + forma base pide a alguien una acción: We need you to send the bank statements. Need + sustantivo solo indica lo que hace falta: I need the statements. Only acota la petición: We only need documents from the last year. En tercera persona de presente simple, need añade -s solo en he, she: He needs the list.

examples.es: We need you to send the bank statements for the last six months.
examples.en: Necesitamos que nos envíe los extractos bancarios de los últimos seis meses.

examples.es: I need to send the supplier list today.
examples.en: Necesito enviar la lista de proveedores hoy.

lessons.title: Classify business transactions
lessons.objective: Clasificar en inglés una compra de negocio según su categoría y su finalidad, usando for y as con verbos de clasificación.
lessons.focus: For para finalidad o destinatario y as para la categoría, con is classified as y counts as.

words.note: Bien de larga duración usado en el negocio.
Categoría que recibe una operación en las cuentas.
Costo para mantener un bien en funcionamiento.
Bien o servicio que el negocio adquiere.
Cuenta donde se registra un gasto.
Reducción del valor registrado de un bien con el tiempo.
Trabajo que devuelve un bien a su estado de uso.
Plan de ingresos y gastos esperados.
Razón por la que se hace una compra.
Documento que prueba una operación.
For + pregunta por la finalidad.

words.es: The oven is for the main kitchen.
words.en: El horno es para la cocina principal.

words.note: Pay + cantidad + for + cosa: pay 4,500 dollars for the oven.

words.es: Is it a repair or a fixed asset purchase?
words.en: ¿Es una reparación o una compra de activo fijo?

lessons.speaking: Habla con el dueño de un horno nuevo. Confirma la categoría contable, pregunta para qué es y decide si es una reparación o un activo fijo. Repite la categoría y la finalidad, y acuerda el siguiente paso.
lessons.partnerRole: Dueño de restaurante que compró un horno nuevo y quiere saber cómo aparecerá en las cuentas.
lessons.openingLine: I bought a new oven for the kitchen. How should I record it?

grammar.focus: For indica la finalidad o el destinatario: The oven is for the main kitchen. As indica la categoría: it counts as a fixed asset; it is classified as a fixed asset. Con pay, la cantidad va antes de for: we paid 4,500 dollars for the oven.

examples.es: The oven is for the main kitchen.
examples.en: El horno es para la cocina principal.

examples.es: The oven counts as a fixed asset, not a repair.
examples.en: El horno cuenta como activo fijo, no como reparación.

lessons.title: Record a journal entry
lessons.objective: Explicar en inglés qué registra un asiento contable y confirmar fecha, importe y justificante usando la voz pasiva.
lessons.focus: Voz pasiva en presente simple con is o are y el participio: The payment is recorded.

words.note: Registro de cargos y abonos de una operación.
Una línea de un asiento o de un documento.
Lado izquierdo de un asiento.
Lado derecho de un asiento.
Día en que ocurrió la operación.
Cantidad de dinero de un documento.
Prueba que respalda una operación.
Cuenta del libro mayor con su número o nombre.
Registrar una operación en las cuentas.
Comprobación antes de contabilizar o cerrar.

words.es: The payment is recorded in the supplier account.
words.en: El pago se registra en la cuenta del proveedor.

words.es: Does the amount match the supporting document?
words.note: Does + sujeto + match: pregunta de presente simple.

words.es: Please confirm the transaction date before posting.
words.en: Confirma la fecha de la operación antes de contabilizar, por favor.
words.note: En inglés no hay tú ni usted; please suaviza la petición entre compañeros y con clientes.

words.es: The entries are posted at the close of the day.
words.en: Los asientos se contabilizan al cierre del día.

lessons.speaking: Explica a un compañero un asiento de pago a un proveedor. Di la fecha, el importe, la cuenta de débito y de crédito y el justificante. Pide que confirme antes de registrar.
lessons.partnerRole: Compañero que revisa los asientos antes de registrarlos en el libro mayor.
lessons.openingLine: I need to record a supplier payment entry. Can you confirm the details with me?

grammar.focus: La voz pasiva se forma con is o are más el participio: The payment is recorded in the supplier account. Se usa cuando la acción importa más que quien la hace. Con sujeto plural cambia a are: The entries are posted every day. El participio de los verbos regulares termina en -ed.

examples.es: The payment is recorded in the supplier account.
examples.en: El pago se registra en la cuenta del proveedor.

examples.es: The entries are posted at the end of each day.
examples.en: Los asientos se contabilizan al final de cada día.

lessons.title: Read a ledger with a coworker
lessons.objective: Leer un libro mayor con un compañero y explicar cómo una operación cambió una cuenta, usando el pasado simple para el hecho y el pasado continuo para el contexto.
lessons.focus: Pasado continuo (was closing, were reviewing) para una acción en curso y pasado simple (arrived, dropped) para el hecho que la interrumpe; los verbos de estado como owe no van en continuo.

words.note: Registro de todas las cuentas de la entidad.
Línea registrada en el libro mayor.
Saldo al comienzo del periodo.
Saldo al final del periodo.
Cambio registrado en una cuenta.
Importes que los clientes deben al negocio.
Entrada de dinero recibida por una deuda.
Dinero entregado para saldar una deuda.
Comparar dos registros hasta que coincidan.
Cambio hecho para corregir un saldo.

words.es: What was the balance before the entry?
words.en: ¿Cuál era el saldo antes del asiento?
words.note: Con be, la pregunta en pasado invierte sujeto y verbo: What was the balance?

lessons.speaking: Lee una línea del libro mayor con un compañero. Explica cuál era el saldo antes del asiento, qué cambió la operación y cuál es el saldo ahora. Confirma las cifras y acuerda la revisión.
lessons.partnerRole: Compañero que revisa una línea del libro mayor después de que se registró una operación.
lessons.openingLine: There is a ledger entry I do not understand. Can we look at it together?

grammar.focus: El pasado continuo (was closing, were reviewing) describe una acción en curso cuando ocurrió otra: I was closing the report when the payment arrived. El pasado simple marca el hecho. Los verbos de estado como owe, have o know no se usan en continuo: the client still owed 5,000 dollars.

examples.es: I was closing the weekly report when the payment arrived.
examples.en: Estaba cerrando el informe semanal cuando llegó el pago.

examples.es: The payment arrived yesterday, and the balance dropped to 3,800 dollars.
examples.en: El pago llegó ayer y el saldo bajó a 3.800 dólares.

lessons.title: Match an invoice to a payment
lessons.objective: Comparar en inglés el número de factura, la referencia del pago, la fecha y el importe, y explicar una diferencia usando el present perfect con already, yet y still.
lessons.focus: Present perfect (I have compared, the payment has arrived) con already, yet y still para acciones que siguen relevantes.

words.note: Identificador impreso en la factura.
Código que vincula un pago con una factura.
Cifra de dinero de un documento.
Fecha en que los fondos cuentan para el saldo.
Diferencia entre dos datos que deberían coincidir.
Comparación de dos registros para que coincidan.
Dinero recibido para una factura.
Factura que aún no se ha pagado o conciliado.
Prueba del banco de que un pago se envió o recibió.
Cuenta bancaria para pagos diarios.

words.es: I have compared the invoice number with the reference.
words.en: He comparado el número de factura con la referencia.

words.es: Does the amount match the invoice?
The payment has already arrived with a different date.
words.en: El pago ya ha llegado con otra fecha.

words.es: The reference does not match the invoice.
words.en: La referencia no coincide con la factura.

lessons.speaking: Cruza una factura con un pago con una clienta. Compara número, referencia, fecha e importe en voz alta, indica qué coincide y cuál no. Acuerden la siguiente verificación.
lessons.partnerRole: Clienta que cree que una factura está pagada pero el banco muestra otra referencia.
lessons.openingLine: We paid last month's invoice, but your records still show it as outstanding. Can you check?

grammar.focus: El present perfect usa have o has más el participio: I have compared the number, the payment has arrived. Already va antes del participio o al final: The payment has already arrived. Yet va al final en preguntas o negativas: Has the payment arrived yet? Still indica que algo sigue igual: The reference is still missing.

examples.es: I have compared the invoice number with the bank reference.
examples.en: He comparado el número de factura con la referencia del banco.

examples.es: The payment has already arrived, but with a different date.
examples.en: El pago ya ha llegado, pero con otra fecha.

lessons.title: Follow up on an unpaid invoice
lessons.objective: Preguntar a un cliente en inglés cuándo pagará una factura vencida y acordar cómo resolver una partida en disputa, usando will para compromisos y hope con presente simple.
lessons.focus: Will para compromisos firmes, hope + presente simple para expectativas y la pregunta cuándo con when.

words.note: Factura que supera su fecha de pago.
Línea que el cliente no acepta.
Parte del importe que el cliente acepta.
Día en que se espera el pago.
Mensaje que pide un pago.
Tiempo permitido para pagar una factura.
Interés por pagar tarde, cuando la ley o el contrato lo permite.
Plan con fechas acordadas para pagar.
Servicio facturado pero no realizado.
Persona o empresa que debe el pago.

words.es: When do you expect to pay the invoice?
words.note: Expect + to + verbo pregunta por una intención o un plan.

words.es: I hope the payment arrives before Friday.
words.en: Espero que el pago llegue antes del viernes.
words.note: En inglés, hope va con presente simple, no con subjuntivo: I hope it arrives.

words.es: We will pay the undisputed part on Monday.
words.en: Pagaremos la parte no disputada el lunes.

words.es: We will review the disputed line separately.
words.en: Revisaremos la partida disputada por separado.

lessons.speaking: Haz seguimiento de una factura de más de treinta días. Pregunta cuándo se pagará, nombra la partida en disputa y acuerda si el cliente pagará la parte no disputada ahora y revisará el resto por separado. Cierra con la fecha acordada.
lessons.partnerRole: Cliente con una factura atrasada que disputa una línea por un servicio que no se prestó.
lessons.openingLine: Good morning, I am calling about the invoice that is a month overdue. When do you expect to pay it?

grammar.focus: Will expresa un compromiso firme: I will pay the undisputed part on Monday. Hope seguido de presente simple expresa una expectativa: I hope the client pays before Friday.
